location: Design Notes > Worker interface ('the version process SIGTERMs and reaps its workers in a finally before teardown') vs 'On its own SIGTERM ... waits at most 10 s ... SIGKILLs the rest'
issue: Only the stop path has a bound: wait at most 10 s, then SIGKILL. The generic `finally` reap has none. It runs on any other exit while workers are alive, for example an exception while spawning the second worker, merging a result or re-recording timings, a KeyboardInterrupt in a direct run, or a `getppid` race. That reap is a plain SIGTERM-and-wait. A worker that got `JobStopped` 'ignores further SIGTERM', so if its Playwright teardown hangs, nothing ever kills it.
implementation_impact: An implementer can write `p.terminate(); p.wait()` in the `finally`. The version process then blocks forever before `_teardown`: the PS container and its `psm.slots` label stay up, ps-run-layer waits on the child with no timeout, and the job hangs until someone runs `--stop-job`. A second implementer may reuse the 10 s bound instead, so the two exit paths behave differently and no test pins either one.
suggestion: Define one reap helper for every exit path: SIGTERM the workers still alive, wait at most 10 s in total, SIGKILL the rest, then wait for them. Both the stop path and the generic `finally` call it. Add a unit test in which a stub worker ignores SIGTERM and the version process still reaches teardown in about 10 s.

location: Design Notes > Snapshot and reset in shell ('failure = timeout, exception, non-zero exit or missing sentinel') / Confirmation passes ('sets that phase's END outcome to `<sub-phase>-failed`')
issue: The spec gives the END outcome only for the enclosing `rerun-seq:<engine>` phase. It never says what a failing sub-phase records for itself in `boot_phases` (`snapshot-db`, `reset-db`, `reset-files`, `reset-opcache`, or `wait-http#n` with no response). `fl.phase.__exit__` records `ok` unless `ph.status` is set or an exception escapes the `with` block. A non-zero `_exec` exit, a missing sentinel, or a `TimeoutExpired` caught inside the block therefore records `{outcome: 'ok'}`. In parallel mode, when the snapshot fails and no engine needs a pass, that outcome is the only trace of the failure in the record.
implementation_impact: `boot_phases` can claim `snapshot-db: ok` or `reset-db: ok` for a step that failed, and the progress log shows `END reset-db ok` right before a `parallel-unconfirmed` verdict. Tests for the Unconfirmable and Sequential reset fails rows cannot pin the value, so implementers will pick different strings (`ok`, `failed`, `error(...)`, `timeout`).
suggestion: State that each failing sub-phase sets its own END outcome: `timeout` on TimeoutExpired, otherwise a fixed `failed` (or `<reason>`), and for `wait-http` `no-response`. Add these outcomes to the Unconfirmable, Sequential reset fails and snapshot-failure unit assertions on `boot_phases`.

location: Design Notes > Phases ('`{browser}` = `<engine>-seq` comes from a separate `ctx['browser_token']` ... Sequential passes also set `ctx['screenshot_dir']` ...; the sequential fallback keeps today's `<shots>/<ver>`') and Tasks > docs (quickstart: '`{browser}` = `<engine>-seq` in sequential passes')
issue: The spec says which passes use the `<engine>-seq` screenshot dir, but not which passes set `browser_token`. The sequential fallback is contrasted only on the screenshot dir. Its later engines run after the same shared reset routine as a confirmation pass, so 'post-reset pass → `-seq` token' is a plausible reading. The quickstart line 'in sequential passes' will be read by module authors who know `--sequential-browsers` as covering that mode too.
implementation_impact: One implementer sets `browser_token` on every in-process pass that follows a reset, including the sequential fallback's later engines; another sets it only on `rerun-seq` and BO-login fallback passes. Specs that build data names from `{browser}` then produce different data and expected text depending on the slot-admission mode, which affects the Identical findings comparison, and the docs promise a behaviour the code may not have.
suggestion: Add one sentence: `browser_token` is set only for `rerun-seq` and BO-login fallback passes; the lockstep worker pass, single-engine runs and every engine of the sequential fallback expand `{browser}` to the bare engine name. In the quickstart, write 'in the confirmation passes after a parallel run (`rerun-seq`, BO-login fallback)' instead of 'in sequential passes'.

location: Design Notes > Worker interface ('Workers check `os.getppid()` in the lock and barrier polls and exit when the parent is gone') and the spec.json schema
issue: spec.json carries no parent PID, so the spec gives nothing to compare `os.getppid()` against. The obvious shortcut, `getppid() == 1`, is wrong whenever a child subreaper exists, for example a systemd user manager, a process supervisor, or tini/dumb-init in a dev container. An orphan is then reparented to the subreaper's PID, not 1. The spec also doesn't say whether a worker that detects parent death writes a result, or with what exit code it exits.
implementation_impact: With the `== 1` check, an orphaned worker whose version process was SIGKILLed never notices. It polls `lock-wait` or `barrier-wait` forever, since neither has a timeout, and keeps a live Playwright browser and a holder marker. That is exactly the leak this check exists to prevent.
suggestion: Add `parent_pid` to spec.json, written by the version process as `os.getpid()`. A worker treats `os.getppid() != parent_pid` as parent gone, removes its holder marker best-effort, writes no result and exits with a fixed code (e.g. 1). Add a unit test that kills the version-process stub and checks that the worker exits within a few `LOCKSTEP_POLL`s.

location: Tasks & Acceptance > tests ('lock and barrier with real `flock`/files across threads') vs Design Notes > Worker interface (worker calls `fl.progress_attach`, `job_register`, `timing_activate`)
issue: The worker's lock-wait and barrier-wait phases go through process-global state: `fl.phase` records into `_TIMING['sink']`, a single global that `timing_activate()` replaces, and it also uses `_PROGRESS` and `_JOB`. `job_register` installs a SIGTERM handler, which raises ValueError outside the main thread and is swallowed. Two simulated workers running as threads in one process therefore share one timing sink, so the second `timing_activate()` discards the first thread's sink. The spec doesn't say what the threaded test exercises: the worker entry point, or lower-level lock and barrier helpers that take explicit paths and a sink.
implementation_impact: A test that runs the worker main in two threads gets mixed or lost `lock-wait:<engine>` and `barrier-wait:<engine>` timings and a shared progress version. It becomes flaky, or the implementer bends the production code to fit the test, for example per-thread sinks that the real process path never uses. The spec's phase-timing claims (suffixes per engine, `TimingSink.events` order) are then not covered by any deterministic test.
suggestion: Name the seam. Lock acquire/release and barrier wait become helpers such as `_scenario_lock(lock_path, holders_dir, engine, exclusive, parent_pid)` and `_barrier(step_dir, engine, engines, k, parent_pid)`, with no global sink or progress dependence, plus a thin wrapper that opens the `fl.phase`. Only these helpers run across threads. Phase recording and `timings` re-recording are covered by the single real stub-worker subprocess test.
